rules.sentence: Findings of thick, rather than thin, suprapapillary plates and lack of neutrophils in the stratum corneum may help distinguish PRP from psoriasis.
Typically, with PRP, the granular layer is normal or thickened under areas of parakeratosis on histologic evaluation.
While acantholysis may be seen in <25% of cases, this finding can further help distinguish PRP from psoriasis.
Griffiths also suggested that these clinical subtypes were predictive of clinical prognosis, but these predictions were not validated and have not been held in clinical trials.
